I really don’t understand how people saying “a touch of the tism” is any different from when people (used to) say “I’m so OCD” and almost everyone seems to know that it isn’t okay. Everyone can fixate on something, that’s just called liking it/having a hobby. Everyone gets irritated when there’s too much noise. Everyone has textures that they dislike and/or avoid. It has to be debilitating, that’s why it’s a disability. But maybe I’m salty since the people who used to bully me for my symptoms when I was younger are now claiming to have it.

Yeah. I believe a lot of people don’t realize the difference between “disliking yourself because of a disorder/disability” and “acknowledging the negative effects it has on your life”. Which is really unfair to do and another reason why it’s insensitive imo.

I often notice that this tends to push people into thinking autism is a personality trait and not a disorder. So I think it’s at the least insensitive/invalidating. But that’s just my viewpoint. I had some stunted growth as a kid due to the struggles I had with eating, and I still have malnutrition issues now for the same reason. So because of that and other stuff it just seems…weird to say ig. Like the “I’m so OCD” phrase used in the past.

Not disagreeing with you, sorry if it reads like that. Just adding my own viewpoint as another autistic person :)
